subject: Hawthorn trial - success charter, KPIs & ownership
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@hawthorn.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hawthorn trial - initial recap and next steps

Hi Samira (and team),

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we can kick off the 4-week trial with clearly measurable outcomes.

Call highlights:
- Goal: Validate ML-assisted extraction across invoices + purchase orders for the AP workflow; target is 90% structured-extraction F1 on our two gold datasets and sub-200ms p95 latency for single-document inference at peak.
- Data: You confirmed we can use the sandbox feed (anonymized) and a 300-record warmup set to calibrate thresholds.
- Constraints: PCI/PII redaction required, logs must be retained for 30 days, and exportable audit trail is needed for compliance review.

Proposed trial structure (summary):
1) Week 0 (this week): onboarding, access & config (trial-config.yaml attached).
2) Week 1: baseline run with your warmup set — collect latency/throughput and model quality metrics.
3) Week 2: iterate on batching/quantization recommendations + run targeted A/B on two model variants.
4) Week 3: scale run at expected load pattern (peak QPS) and finalize acceptance metrics.
5) Wrap: document results, handoff to your engineering/ops for production planning.

Draft success criteria (details to align below):
- Latency: p95 < 200ms for 1 document / single-request path.
- Throughput: sustained 20 qps with 95% of requests within latency SLOs.
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.002 for the dominant workload (invoice extraction).
- Quality: Structured field extraction F1 >= 90% on the gold set; key-value accuracy >= 92% on the PO set.
- Compliance: Audit logs available and sample redaction verified.

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood trial lead: Rohan Mehta — config, model routing, rollout policy.
- Trial instrumentation & evaluation: Marissa Cole — metrics harness, evaluation datasets, and dashboards.
- Commercial/terms: Ben Carter — trial commercial scope, pricing guardrails.

Next steps: can you confirm the sandbox access by EOD Wednesday (24 Mar)? If yes we’ll schedule an onboarding session (45 min) and share access & the trial charter PDF.

Attachments: trial-config.yaml (config stub) — I’ve attached a short charter PDF we’ll use as the working source of truth.

Thanks,
Rohan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---

Subject: Re: Hawthorn trial - initial recap and next steps

Thanks Rohan — this is great and aligns with our expectations. Quick confirmations:
- Sandbox access: we’ll provision an S3 bucket and a service account by Wednesday EOD (23 Mar).
- Warmup set: the 300 anonymized records are ready; I’ll drop the access details in a separate email to Marissa.
- Compliance: 30-day log retention is fine. We do need a short statement on where logs live (region) for our audit team.

Couple of asks from my side before we kick off:
1) Can you add a simple smoke-check script we can run in our environment to validate end-to-end connectivity?
2) For cost calc: can you show an estimated cost delta if we run with quantized models vs FP16?

If you can address those, we’re set to onboard.

—Samira
Head of AI Product
Hawthorn Analytics

Thanks Samira — appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick replies inline and a concrete ownership map.

Samira: re logs — Redwood will retain trial logs in us-west-2 by default; we’ll provide an export bundle for audit review. I’ll attach a one-page audit summary to the charter.

Requests:
1) Smoke-check script: Marissa, can your team produce a small shell/python snippet that validates auth + an end-to-end transform? Deliverable target: Fri 26 Mar EOD.
2) Cost delta by model type: Ben and I will produce a short estimate (quantized vs FP16) using your expected token mix and expected token-count per invoice.

Refined success metrics (please review):
- Latency: p95 <= 200ms for single-document requests (measured after our prefix caching warmup).
- Throughput: 20 QPS sustained, with <5% dropped/queued requests.
- Cost: <= $0.002/token on the production-like run; we’ll report both raw token cost and normalized cost per document.
- Quality:
  * Extraction F1 (invoices): >= 90%
  * PO key-value accuracy: >= 92%
  * Manual spot-check: sample of 30 docs must show no more than 2 critical failures (mis-extraction of vendor or total).
- Compliance: redaction validated on 10 sample docs; audit bundle produced.

Ownership / action items: 
- Rohan: final config + rollout policy; coordinate region & instance sizing (by 2027-03-26).
- Marissa: instrument evaluation harness, push dashboard to shared Drive, deliver smoke script (by 2027-03-26).
- Ben: finalize trial commercial scope and confirm any promotional credit (by 2027-03-29).

Timeline: Onboarding call (45m) — propose Thu 25 Mar at 10:00 PT. If that works, I’ll send calendar invite.

I’ll also attach the first draft of the trial charter to this thread — PDF attached.

Best,
Rohan

Looping in the evaluation plan and what I’ll deliver by end of week:

What I’ll ship (deliverables):
- Evaluation harness (Python) that computes per-field precision/recall/F1, and overall doc-level accuracy. It will output CSV and JSON artifacts for the dashboard.
- Smoke-check script (bin/smoke_check.sh) that you can run from your CI to validate auth + a sample transform.
- Dashboard: Looker dashboard stub in the shared Drive (link above) — will include latency P95, QPS, cost/token, and extraction F1 over time.
- Datasets: I’ll upload the 300 warmup docs + 2 evaluation gold sets (invoice_gold_v1.jsonl, po_gold_v1.jsonl) to the Drive folder.

Instrumentation notes:
- Metrics to capture server-side: request_id, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, outcome_code, extraction_f1, charges_token_cost_usd.
- We’ll tag trial runs with trial_id=HW-8342 so we can filter dashboards.

Open questions for Hawthorn:
- For the quality gate, do you prefer micro-averaged F1 or macro-averaged F1 for the fields? We recommend micro-F1 for skewed field distributions.

Delivery targets: all artifacts by EOD Mon 29 Mar so Ben can include final commercial notes in the trial statement.

-Marissa
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
